question: Identify the gas that is evolved when magnesium and manganese react with nitric acid.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Hydrogen gas**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Magnesium (Mg) and manganese (Mn) react with nitric acid (HNO₃) to produce hydrogen gas (H₂).
 
• The reaction is a redox reaction where magnesium and manganese are oxidized, and nitric acid is reduced.
 
• Hydrogen gas is typically evolved when metals react with acids, releasing H₂ in the process.
 
• Both magnesium and manganese are strong enough reducing agents to release hydrogen gas from nitric acid.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Redox Reactions**

 
 
• Redox reactions involve the transfer of electrons between two species. It consists of two half-reactions: oxidation and reduction.
 
• Oxidation refers to the loss of electrons, while reduction refers to the gain of electrons.
 
 
 
• **Properties of Magnesium**
 
 
• Magnesium is a lightweight metal with a silvery-white appearance.
 
• It is highly reactive, especially with acids, and forms hydrogen gas when reacting with most acids.
 
 
 
• **Properties of Manganese**
 
 
• Manganese is a metal with important industrial metal alloy uses, particularly in stainless steels.
 
• It reacts with dilute acids to release hydrogen gas.
 
 
 
• **Nitric Acid**
 
 
• Nitric acid (HNO₃) is a highly corrosive mineral acid.
 
• It is commonly used in the production of fertilizers, explosives, and in various chemical synthesis processes.
